Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to YES Bank's Q2FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call. On the management panel, we have with us today Mr. Vinay M. 
Tonse, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer; Mr. Manish Jain, Executive

As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need 
assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then 
zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
Participants are requested to ask questions pertaining to the bank's Q2 results only. For

Vinay M. Tonse: 
Yes. Thank you. Good morning to all. Thank you for joining us for the quarterly results 
presentation, and also thank you for coming in very early today.  
 
So before we discuss performance for the second quarter FY27, I would like to address 
the Honorable Supreme Court's judgment of 15th October 2026 concerning the INR 
8,415 crores of Additional Tier 1 bonds written down in March 2020. This is a significant 
development for YES Bank, and I believe it is important that we address it upfront. 
 
The Honorable Supreme Court has upheld the Bombay High Court's judgment setting 
aside the AT-1 write-down, and dismissed the appeals filed by YES Bank, the 
Administrator, the Reserve Bank of India, and the Union of India. We respect the 
judgment and are examining it carefully, including the options available to the Bank.  
 
The reconstruction of YES Bank in March 2020 took place in exceptional circumstances 
with the objective of restoring the stability and viability of the institution, and protecting 
the interests of depositors and the wider financial system. The AT-1 write-down was 
one of the measures undertaken in that context. We are evaluating the implications of 
the judgment with the same institutional responsibility that guides our other decisions.  
 
Let me address the capital implications first.  
Based on our current assessment, which is indicative, and as of 30th September 2026, 
the reinstatement of the AT-1 principal amount is expected to have a pro forma impact 
of approximately 240 basis points on our Common Equity Tier 1 ratio, including Profits. 
Our overall Tier 1 capital ratio is expected to remain around 13.7% on a pro forma basis.

We recognize that the distinction between CET-1 and overall Tier 1 capital is important. 
We will continue to assess the implications for our capital structure, regulatory buffers, 
Balance Sheet strength, and future growth plans. 
Capital planning is an ongoing Board-level process. Any capital decisions will be based 
on a careful assessment of regulatory requirements, the cost and availability of capital, 
shareholder interests, and the bank's medium-term growth objectives. We will not pre-
empt those decisions today.  
 
On the legal and accounting aspects, we are examining the judgment in detail, including 
the available legal options and appropriate steps going forward. We will make 
disclosures in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and as the positions 
become clear. 
We also ensure that the treatment of the AT-1 bonds and related accounting matters is 
addressed in accordance with the judgment, the applicable contractual terms, and the 
advice of our legal and other professional advisors. We do not wish to speculate on 
implementation details or timelines before that assessment is complete.  
 
For us, the responsibility is to deal with the consequences of the judgment in a 
disciplined manner while continuing to strengthen the underlying franchise.  
We understand that you will have questions about the capital impact, future Profitability, 
potential capital actions, and the implications for shareholder value. We will address 
these questions as fully as the facts and our disclosure obligations permit without 
getting into the legal interpretation of the judgment, which we are examining.  
 
Having said that, let me call out that directionally, our priorities remain unchanged: 
building sustainable and Profitable growth, strengthening customer relationships, 
maintaining cost discipline, monitoring the quality of our assets, and generating durable 
returns for our shareholders.  
 
With that, let me talk about the quarter's results and the progress we are making across 
our business.  
Q2FY27 Financial Performance 
Getting into the Q2FY27 financial performance. The Bank reported Net Profit of INR 
1,080 crores, an increase of 65% year-on-year. Operating Profit increased by 29.4% 
year-on-year to INR 1,678 crores. Net Interest Income increased by 22.7% year-on-
year to INR 2,822 crores, while the core fees grew by 15.5% year-on-year.  
Return on Assets for the quarter stood at 0.9%, compared with 0.6% in Q2 FY26 and 
0.9% in Q1 FY27. The cost-to-income ratio stood at 64.3%, compared with 67.1% in 
the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

During the quarter, we crossed some critical Balance Sheet milestones. The Total 
Assets crossed INR 5 lakh crores, Deposits crossed INR 3.5 lakh crores, and Advances 
exceeded INR 3 lakh crores.  
 
Now moving to the Balance Sheet and Deposit Franchise  
The Bank mobilized INR 18,575 crores of FCNR(B) Deposits and extended Foreign 
Currency Term Loans of INR 15,215 crores through the IBU at GIFT City. These 
transactions affected the reported growth rates and certain income and expenses lines 
during the quarter. 
Reported Advances grew by 23.7% year-on-year. Excluding the FCTL linked to the 
FCNR mobilization, Advances grew 17.6% year-on-year. The corresponding 
normalized Credit-to-Deposit Ratio, stood at 83.1%. 
Deposits grew by 19.5% year-on-year on an end-of-period basis and by 22.1% on an 
average quarterly balance basis. Retail and branch-led Deposits increased by 20.9% 
year-on-year and constituted 58.8% of the total Deposits. On an average quarterly 
balance basis, CASA Deposits grew by 15.5% year-on-year, with growth of 21.8% in 
Current Account balances and 11.6% in Savings Account balances.  
Moving to the margins  
Net Interest Margin for the quarter stood at 2.6%. The sequential moderation of 
approximately 12 to 14 basis points was largely attributable to the FCNR(B) mobilization 
and the associated liquidity and deployment profile. The Bank will continue to focus on 
calibrated deployment of available liquidity and the composition and cost of incremental 
Deposits.  
 
Moving to the Fees and Operating Expenses  
Non-interest Income increased by 14.4% year-on-year and 4.7% sequentially. Core 
fees increased by 15.5% Y-o-Y, supported by growth in trade and cash management, 
loan processing fees, and card product fees. The sequential growth in loan processing 
fees included some associated with the Foreign Currency Term Loans and was 
substantially offset by related FCNR mobilization costs.  
Operating expenses increased by 14.2% Y-o-Y and 5.1% sequentially to INR 3,026 
crores. The quarter included INR 51 crores of commissions on foreign currency 
borrowings linked to the FCNR(B) mobilization, INR 20 crores of marketing expenditure 
relating to the Asian Games sponsorship, and INR 31 crores arising from changes in 
central and state wage codes. Excluding these items, operating expenses were broadly 
stable on a sequential basis.  
 
Moving to the Asset Quality and business mix

Asset Quality indicators remained stable. The gross and net NPA ratios stood at 1.2% 
and 0.2% respectively, and both improved Y-o-Y. Gross slippages were 1.3% of 
Advances, broadly unchanged sequentially. The net credit cost for the quarter was 0.3% 
of average assets, similar to Q1 FY27. The Bank also recognized P&L gains of INR 395 
crores from the Security Receipts portfolio during the quarter. The rise in standard asset 
provision was primarily driven by increase in loan balances, including the FCTL portion.  
Growth was distributed across the bank's principal business segments. Retail asset 
disbursement increased by 35% Y-o-Y, with the Retail book growth inching up to nearly 
9%. Commercial Banking Advances grew 20.2%, while Corporate and Institutional 
Banking Advances grew by 31.4% year-on-year.  
Capital and liquidity 
And on a reported basis, before considering the pro forma impact of the AT-1 judgment 
discussed earlier, the CET-1 ratio stood at 13.7%, and the liquidity coverage ratio stood 
at 131.4%.  
 
To conclude, our priorities remain centered on improving core Profitability, growing 
Advances and Deposits in a risk-calibrated manner, deepening the granular deposit 
franchise, managing margins and operating efficiency, and maintaining Asset Quality. 
Capital planning will remain an important area of focus as we assess the implications 
of the judgment and support the Bank's future growth requirements. 
The Bank has made progress in strengthening the scale and quality of its franchise. At 
the same time, we recognize the significance of the Supreme Court judgment and the 
need for a carefully considered response. We will continue to act in accordance with 
applicable legal and regulatory requirements, engage with the regulator and other 
authorities as appropriate, and keep the market appropriately informed.
